bull.b: Near-zero debt reduces interest obligations and financial leverage while preserving flexibility to allocate capital toward clinical development. This provides a stronger balance-sheet foundation than heavily indebted peers, although the company remains dependent on funding because it has not reached commercial profitability.

The substantial increase in cash provides resources to continue research, clinical trials, and corporate operations over the coming periods. A stronger liquidity position can reduce immediate financing pressure and allow management to advance NVG-291 while pursuing longer-term development milestones.

The ATM program creates an established, flexible channel for raising capital as funding needs arise rather than requiring one immediate financing event. That can support continued pipeline investment and operational continuity, though future share issuance would dilute existing holders.

bear.b: NervGen has no recurring product revenue to offset its development expenses, while losses are increasing materially. This limits internal funding capacity and means future financial performance remains dependent on successful clinical development, regulatory progress, and eventual commercialization.

Persistently negative and worsening operating cash flow indicates that the business consumes substantial capital to sustain research and development. Continued acceleration in burn could shorten the effective funding horizon and increase reliance on equity issuance or other external financing.

The planned restatement exposes accounting and internal-control challenges that can weaken confidence in reported historical results and increase compliance workload. Although the identified adjustments are non-cash and do not affect liquidity or operations, repeated reporting corrections may complicate investor assessment.
